insights.insight: The protocol settles attribution at ~$0.10 per verified receipt versus $5–$150 CPA for probabilistic ad tech — a 50–200x cost delta driven by eliminating the attribution problem entirely, not optimizing around it.

With Chrome completing cookie deprecation and device fingerprinting increasingly blocked, the ad industry has no cross-ecosystem, identity-free purchase signal at scale — this dataset of 4,079 cryptographically verified receipts across $236K GMV represents a structural alternative, not an incremental one.

Amazon knows Amazon purchases; Walmart knows Walmart purchases; neither knows the other — this protocol aggregates cross-ecosystem purchase data from email receipts without requiring any platform to open its silo, which no first-party data strategy can replicate.

insights.topic: Rural and non-metro coverage as competitive moat
insights.insight: Sixteen active CBSAs now include confirmed non-metro adoption across CA, ID, WI, and PA — geographies that probabilistic ad tech systematically underserves due to urban data density bias, making this a rare verified signal source for brands with national or rural distribution.

Category entropy sits at 3.131 bits and is stable — the verified purchase basket is spreading across grocery, home improvement, QSR, services (AAA), and dev infrastructure rather than concentrating, which matters for brands assessing whether this signal set covers their category.

insights.topic: Merchant resolution gap masks premium spend
insights.insight: Eleven percent of receipts fail merchant name resolution, yet the 'Unknown' category carries the highest average basket at $133.50 — meaning brand-level analysis is currently undercounting a premium spend segment that cryptographic verification still confirms as real purchase events.
